T5: rendering runs through the owned worker (core/process) into a per-attempt staging folder with policy wall-clock and memory limits and an onCreated identity hook; returns the verified unpublished output; publication and job state moved to core/jobs.ts (the in-memory RenderQueue is removed); input protocols restricted to file. Inputs are restricted to the accepted container formats (MEDIA_FORMATS) as well.
T6: audio clips apply schema-bounded gain (volume) and linear fades (afade) in clip time before placement.

T7: renders only from a versioned render plan (core/render/plan.ts): filter values formatted from integer ticks, input files verified against the plan asset hashes, titles drawn by one ASS script through libass with the pinned, hash-verified fonts (the drawtext title path and host-font lookup are removed), a fit check refuses titles wider than the frame, and a probe receipt records the plan hash.

T7 review: each clip reads its own seeked input (-ss/-t), resolved by the plan asset hash and size; the title script must match the plan hash; one wall-clock limit covers the capability probe, fit check and render; the fit check reads margin bands of a quarter-size frame sampled once per title; audio is made 48 kHz stereo and placed by an exact sample delay; the receipt records the libass API version.

T8: renders any window of a plan (the whole plan for export, one frame as PNG or a short segment as MP4 for reference preview) with absolute timeline timestamps, so the plan's title script times titles in any window; timestamp offsets are rounded to the nearest tick from exact flicks (setpts truncates); clips are cut one frame long and ended by the overlay enable window; audio is shaped in clip time, then cut to the window.

T8a review: each source frame keeps its own timeline time (clip start plus its distance from the clip source start) in export and in any window, with up to two frames of lead-in, so the frame-rate filter selects the same source frame for every output frame at any source rate; renders take an optional wall-clock limit; RENDERER_VERSION versions how plans are drawn.

T8a review 2: the lead-in is bounded by the source (not the clip), so the source frame covering a clip's first instant is always read; clips are placed in a one-tick-per-flick time base (settb) so offsets are exact for any source time base, including looped stills.

T9c: the render worker runs sandboxed (restricted, low-integrity token) and may write only to its own worker/ subfolder, named in the worker request; only the main data stream of what it wrote is kept, copied by keepMainStream into a file the service creates in the staging folder the worker could never write, so neither the worker's permissions (on its file or its folder) nor alternate streams reach a published file.

Resource policy v2 (agent decision, 2026-10-13): -threads is an FFmpeg per-input option, so every render input now gets renderThreads before its -i (the single global -threads, which bound only the first input, is removed) and the libx264 encoder takes the policy value; decoded frames and the encoder are unchanged, so rendered output and RENDERER_VERSION are unaffected.

Worker read containment (2026-10-13): each render and title-fit worker declares the files it reads (its inputs, titles.ass and the fonts folder), which procd grants to the worker's own AppContainer capability for its lifetime; rendering itself is unchanged.

W5.1 (2026-10-21): title staging writes a pinned fonts.conf (core/render/fontconfig.ts) and passes FONTCONFIG_FILE to FFmpeg workers through procd's allowlisted workerEnv; fit-check and render workers read fonts.conf.
R8 (2026-10-21): Windows mediaTools prefer vendor/ffmpeg-win64-r8 (libass fontconfig, DirectWrite disabled); EXTERNAL_BINARY_PINS hash-gate the bundle; procd stages sibling DLLs with the exe.
